paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: : The performance on Llama3.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of six different methods—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 10^3 (i.e., 1 to 1000). The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", ranges from 60% to 80% with major tick marks every 5 percentage points. Each method is represented by a distinct line with a unique color and marker: Base (black circles), FT (blue inverted triangles), IKE (red upward triangles), MEND (brown diamonds), MEMIT (purple circles), and ROME (green squares). All lines show an increasing trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases. At the lowest co-occurrence number (1), ROME starts at approximately 73%, MEND and MEMIT are around 67%, IKE is at about 65%, FT is at roughly 63%, and Base is at approximately 61%. At the highest co-occurrence number (1000), ROME reaches about 77.5%, MEND and MEMIT are near 73%, IKE is at around 70%, FT is at approximately 68%, and Base is at about 66.5%. The green line (ROME) consistently achieves the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence values, followed by MEND and MEMIT, while Base remains the lowest throughout.
